title: RBAC v2 migration: observability-driven validation and admin rollback strategy
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Execute a low-risk migration from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 across hosted and Dedicated fleets with full audit log continuity, SSO/SAML compatibility checks, and a tested admin rollback path. This ticket coordinates the observability gates, validation hooks, and emergency rollback choreography needed for cutover weekends and customer communication windows.
background: RBAC v2 introduces fine-grained role assertions and a new role mapping store. Previous cutover attempts identified gaps in audit completeness and sporadic mapping regressions for SSO-mapped users. We need a migration plan that combines dual-write, incremental backfills, preflight validation, and a reversible switchover so customers with complex SAML mappings are not impacted.
decisions: Use dual-write (v1 -> v2) with a 72-hour observation window before enabling read-path on v2 for canary accounts.
Backfill will be queued and rate-limited by tenant to avoid DB I/O spike; prefer streaming backfill with resume tokens over batch dump/restore.
Audit log schema will include a 'rbac_migration_tag' to correlate events across v1 and v2 during the observation window.
Fallback path will rely on traffic routing to a v1-compatible API gateway and an automated role-sync job to reconcile in-flight changes.
Require security review sign-off and SOC/TDR stakeholders to validate audit retention and KMS access for logs prior to full cutover.
migration_steps: Step 1: Enable dual-write for write-after-commit paths in staging; validate eventual consistency within 30s for 95% of events.
Step 2: Start tenant-scoped streaming backfill for historical role assignments; throttle to 100 tenants/hour with concurrency 4.
Step 3: Run SSO/SAML mapping verification job for top 50 customers by active MAU; surface mismatches as blocking defects.
Step 4: Promote v2 read-path for internal canary orgs during a low-traffic window, monitor for 6 hours.
Step 5: Gradual canary expansion (10% hostnames -> 30% -> 60%) with gating based on audit completeness and unauthorized error delta.
Step 6: Full cutover night with 1 hour of freeze, on-call and platform-ops present for rollback window.
Step 7: Post-cutover reconciliation run and 14-day increased-logging window for regression detection.
backfill_strategy: Streaming tenant-by-tenant backfill using changefeed + resume tokens. Backfills will record a progress checkpoint per tenant in a migration table and expose progress via the migration dashboard. In-flight writes during backfill are handled via dual-write, with last-writer-wins tie-breaker configured to use commit timestamp.
dual_write_strategy: Dual-write implemented at service layer with idempotent writes and an observability flag. Each dual-write emits an audit event to the migration topic; events include rbac_migration_tag and trace_id. A compensating reconciler runs hourly for tenants with >0 mismatch errors.
cutover_plan: Pre-cutover checklist completed and signed: security, legal, customer-success notified.
Maintenance window announced: 02:00–04:00 UTC; canaries staged the previous day.
Freeze external config changes 4 hours prior to window.
Switch read-path to v2 gateway for targeted hostnames; keep v1 gateway healthy for fallback.
Monitor live indicators for 2 hours before expanding traffic.
If thresholds breached, trigger rollback playbook and notify customers in the impacted cohort.
rollback_plan: Immediate traffic switch: revert read-path routing to v1 gateway (automated runbook, <2 minutes target).
Disable v2 read-path for affected tenant prefixes and pause backfill workers for those tenants.
Run role-sync reconciler to ensure v1 state aligns with durable v1 store; surface any v2-only assignments for manual review.
Capture post-rollback audit snapshot and open incident with tag INCIDENT-RBAC-V2 for RCA.
Communicate to customers: brief advisory + follow-up timeline within 2 business days.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: rbac.authorization.unauthorized.rate — alert if p95 increases >3x baseline during canary.
Metric: rbac.audit.event.latency — alert if median >500ms or tail >2s for >5 minutes.
Audit completeness: compare v1 vs v2 event counts per tenant; alert if mismatch >0.5% over 30m.
SSO mapping errors: alert on identity-mapper.failures >5 in 10m for a tenant.
Dashboard links will be created for cross-team visibility; oncall rota assigned for cutover weekend.
acceptance_criteria: All top-50 customers show 0 SSO mapping mismatches after verification job.
Audit events for role changes are present in both v1 and v2 for a continuous 72-hour window for canaries.
No customer-facing 5xx errors or elevated unauthorized spikes during canary expansion beyond alert thresholds.
Security & SOC sign-off recorded in Confluence and ticket marked as 'security_review_required: true'.
Rollback playbook tested end-to-end in staging with an automated run and documented timings.
notes: We intentionally avoid changing semantic role names during migration to reduce mapping complexity.
Plan assumes KMS access for audit export; ops must confirm key rotation windows do not coincide with cutover.
Customer success will run pre-cutover briefings for top-10 customers with active enterprise contracts.
